0.long_answer: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome is a congenital condition characterized by the underdevelopment or absence of the uterus and sometimes the upper portion of the vagina. Despite the absence of these key reproductive structures, the ovaries are typically functioning normally, which allows for the development of secondary sexual characteristics such as breast development and pubic hair. This condition is one of the most common causes of primary amenorrhea in females who exhibit normal pubertal development, and it is usually diagnosed during adolescence when menstrual periods fail to begin.
